deraux_2018.title: Non-arithmetic ball quotients from a configuration of elliptic curves in an Abelian surface
exact_supported_facts: A=C^2/Lambda with Lambda=(Z+i*sqrt(2)Z)^2 and finite linear part G12 of order 48
the affine element R1*R2*R3 has linear part regular elliptic of order 8 with eigenvalues zeta8 and zeta8^3
Table 2 gives a representative fixed point p=(1/2,(1+i*sqrt(2))/2) for the cyclic order-8 stabilizer <R1*R2*R3>
the order-8 isolated-fixed-point orbit has size 48/8=6

koziarz_rito_roulleau.title: The Bolza curve and some orbifold ball quotient surfaces
locators: Section 4 around the comparison of H48 and G48
exact_supported_facts: the Bolza curve is embedded in its Jacobian by Abel-Jacobi with infinity sent to 0
for a curve automorphism a, the induced affine Jacobian action differs from the linear divisor-difference action by the translation [a(infinity)]-[infinity]
the curve-induced H48 action is conjugate to the Deraux G48 action by an automorphism of the Abelian surface
the cited source does not materialize the conjugating automorphism on A[2]

cecotti.title: Symplectic Singularities, Color Confinement, and the Quantum Dirac Sheaf
exact_supported_facts: the Bolza curve y^2=x^5-x has the order-8 automorphism B9: (x,y)->(i*x,exp(i*pi/4)*y)
B9 fixes the branch points 0 and infinity
its holomorphic differential eigenvalues are zeta8 and zeta8^3

fixed_point_difference_lemma.setup: Let f(z)=Lz+t be an affine automorphism of a complex two-torus A=C^2/Lambda, assume f has a fixed point, and let M be the integral H1 action of L.
fixed_point_difference_lemma.consequence: Fix(f) is a torsor under ker(L-I), hence consists of exactly two points p and p+d, where d is the unique nonzero element of ker(L-I).
fixed_point_difference_lemma.two_torsion: Because ker(L-I) has order 2, d is a nonzero A[2] class.
fixed_point_difference_lemma.mod2_characterization: d is the unique nonzero fixed class of M on A[2].

curve_side_specialization.fixed_pair_exhaustive_reason: The order-8 H1 characteristic polynomial is x^4+1, so there are exactly two fixed points on the Jacobian.

deraux_side_specialization.criterion: If the second fixed point q of the source-bound matching order-8 affine element is materialized in the same Deraux lattice coordinates, q-p is the unique nonzero fixed A[2] class. After the marked Deraux-to-retained lattice adapter, that single class selects exactly one of L1,L2,L3.
